segments.label: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Welcome to Room A. Our next speaker is Imani, with Golden paths: platform engineering developers actually use.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: How a small platform team shipped paved roads for deployment and what made developers adopt them.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Imani walks through three golden paths for service creation, deployment and rollback, and the adoption metrics that told the platform team which paths were working.

segments.label: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Welcome to Room B. Our next speaker is Jonas, with HIPAA-ready Kubernetes: what auditors ask for.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Auditors ask the same four things about a cluster that handles health data: logging, encryption, access reviews and vendor paperwork.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Turn on Kubernetes audit logging on day one and keep the logs for six years, because that is what they will ask for.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Encrypt secrets at rest with a managed key, and show the key rotation history in the review.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Hospital security teams will also ask every vendor for a completed security questionnaire before a pilot.

segments.label: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Welcome to Room B. Our next speaker is Lena, with OpenTelemetry in regulated industries.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: At a bank, every new telemetry signal goes through a compliance review before it leaves the building.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: We kept data residency simple: all telemetry stays in one region, and the collector redacts account numbers before export.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Traces were the easiest to approve because they carry timings and service names, not customer data.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Logs were the hardest. We only ship structured logs with an allow-list of fields.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: The result: incident time dropped by a third in the first quarter.

segments.label: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: Did you run the collector as a central gateway for the redaction?

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Yes, one gateway pool per region, so the redaction rules live in one place that auditors can read.

segments.label: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Welcome to Room A. Our next speaker is Nadia, with Rightsizing pods without paging anyone.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: A safe workflow for lowering pod requests and limits and proving the savings.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Nadia shows request and limit tuning driven by usage data, with guardrails that avoid out-of-memory kills, and a monthly review that finance trusts.

segments.label: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Welcome to Room C. Our next speaker is Theo, with Guardrails for autonomous AI agents.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: An agent that acts for a person should see only the data that person would share.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: We give each agent a scoped key, check every outbound item against a policy engine, and fail closed when the policy service is down.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Text from another company's agent is untrusted input. It goes into the prompt as data, never as instructions.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Keep an audit trail of every decision, so a person can see why their agent said no.

segments.label: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: How do you stop prompt injection when two agents negotiate with each other?

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Treat the other agent's message as data in a delimited block, and only let the model pick from IDs you already know.

segments.label: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Welcome to Room A. Our next speaker is Beatriz, with Zero-trust networking for clusters.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Network policy and workload identity patterns that make lateral movement hard.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Beatriz compares network policy, mutual TLS and workload identity, and shows an incremental rollout plan for an existing cluster.

segments.label: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Welcome to Room B. Our next speaker is Arjun, with Scaling the OpenTelemetry Collector.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Sizing, sampling and routing for collectors that handle a large volume of telemetry.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Arjun explains agent versus gateway collectors, tail sampling trade-offs and the dashboards he uses to watch the pipeline itself.

segments.label: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Welcome to Room A. Our next speaker is Priya, with Cutting the cloud bill with eBPF.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Our cloud bill grew forty percent in a year, and nobody could say which services were responsible.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: We used eBPF to count requests and bytes per pod at the kernel, which gave us a cost map without changing a single service.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: The first surprise was idle capacity: a third of our deployments handled almost no traffic outside business hours.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: The second was chatty services calling each other thousands of times per page view.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Measurement has a cost too, so we kept the eBPF probes to a sampled set and stayed under half a percent of CPU.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: In six months we cut spend by twenty-eight percent, and the savings held because the dashboards stayed on.

segments.label: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: How did you prove the savings to finance before the invoices came in?

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: We priced each idle replica at the on-demand rate and showed finance the forecast next to the actual bill every month.

segments.label: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: Did older kernel versions on some nodes block the eBPF rollout?

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Two node pools were too old, so we upgraded them first. Everything since then has had BTF.

segments.label: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Welcome to Room C. Our next speaker is Ken, with Hybrid search over operational data.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Our operations team searches shipment records all day, and keyword search alone kept missing the right record.

segments.label: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: I run the data platform, so I will show how we index the records. Every shipment event becomes one document with the carrier, the route and free-text notes.

segments.label: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: We added a semantic field next to the text field and merge both result lists with reciprocal rank fusion.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Here is the difference: a search for frozen goods stuck at the border now finds notes that say refrigerated cargo held at customs.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Nobody had to learn a query language. People type the question the way they would ask a colleague.

segments.label: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: Filters still matter. We always filter on the customer and the date range first, and then rank.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Hybrid search cut our time to the right record from minutes to seconds.

segments.label: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Welcome to Room A. Our next speaker is Camille, with Running a platform team of five.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Staffing, on-call and roadmap habits that let a small platform team support hundreds of services.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Camille covers intake, saying no, and measuring developer satisfaction when the team is small.

segments.label: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Welcome to Room C. Our next speaker is Wei, with Agent-to-agent protocols in practice.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: What worked and what broke when companies let their agents exchange information.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Wei reviews message formats, consent steps and how to keep each side's private data out of the exchange.

segments.label: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Welcome to Room B. Our next speaker is Dev, with Zero-code tracing with eBPF on Kubernetes.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: eBPF lets us run small, verified programs inside the Linux kernel, so we can watch every request without touching application code.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: That is what zero-code tracing means: no SDK, no sidecar and no redeploy of your services.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: On Kubernetes we run one agent per node as a DaemonSet, and it attaches eBPF probes to the network and TLS functions of every pod.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: From those probes we rebuild HTTP and gRPC requests, measure latency, and stitch them into traces across services.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: The trace context comes from the headers on the wire, so spans from eBPF line up with spans from your existing OpenTelemetry SDKs.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Now the live demo. This sample shop has six microservices and none of them is instrumented.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Within a minute of installing the agent we see the full call graph and the slow checkout call, all from eBPF.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Where eBPF cannot help: it does not see inside a process, so business attributes like a cart ID still need a line of SDK code.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Kernel versions matter too. You want a recent kernel with BTF, which every major managed Kubernetes now ships.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: So start with eBPF for coverage on day one, and add SDK spans where you need detail.

segments.label: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: How much CPU overhead does eBPF tracing add on small edge nodes, like the computers on our warehouse robots?

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: On small nodes we measured about one to two percent CPU with the default probes. The cost grows with the number of probes, so start with HTTP and DNS and add more once you know your budget.

segments.label: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: Can the same eBPF data show which services sit idle, so we can cut the cloud bill?

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Yes. Request counts per service fall out of the same probes, and idle services stand out within a day.

segments.label: SPEAKER_04
segments.text: Does zero-code tracing still work when the traffic is encrypted with TLS?

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Mostly. We hook the TLS library before encryption, so we see the request, but statically linked binaries need extra probes.

segments.label: SPEAKER_05
segments.text: Does the agent export OpenTelemetry spans directly, or do we still need a collector?

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: It exports OTLP directly, so any OpenTelemetry collector or backend works unchanged.

segments.label: SPEAKER_06
segments.text: Thank you!

segments.label: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Welcome to Room A. Our next speaker is Rosa, with Showback that engineers actually read.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Cost reports teams act on: ownership tags, weekly digests and budgets with context.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Rosa shows how to attribute shared cluster cost to teams and present it where engineers already work.

segments.label: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Welcome to Room C. Our next speaker is Mia, with eBPF on warehouse robots.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Our warehouse robots each run a tiny Kubernetes cluster on a fanless computer, so every percent of CPU matters.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: We set an overhead budget of one percent for observability, and eBPF was the only tracing approach that fit.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Networks on a warehouse floor are flaky, so the agent buffers traces locally and ships them when the robot docks.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: The best bug we found was a retry storm between the navigation and lidar services that only happened near the loading bays.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: If you run eBPF at the edge, pin your kernel version across the fleet, or your probes will break one robot at a time.

segments.label: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: What did you have to turn off to stay under the one percent budget?

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: We dropped DNS tracing and sampled HTTP at ten percent on each robot. Errors are always kept.

segments.label: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: How many robots run this today?

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: About two hundred robots across four warehouses.

segments.label: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Welcome to Room A. Our next speaker is Hana, with Supply-chain security for container images.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Signing, scanning and admission checks that keep untrusted images out of the cluster.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Hana demonstrates image signing and an admission policy, and what to do when a base image is compromised.

segments.label: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Welcome to Room A. Our next speaker is Tom, with Designing conferences for everyone.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Accessible events start with the schedule: fewer parallel tracks, longer breaks and a quiet room people can find.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Live captions help everyone, not only people who are deaf or hard of hearing. They also help anyone listening in a second language.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Publish talk recordings with captions and timestamps, so people can jump to the part they need.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Ask attendees what would help them before the event, not after.

segments.label: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: Do you caption the questions from the audience too?

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: We do. The moderator repeats each question into the microphone, so the captions pick it up.

segments.label: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Welcome to Room B. Our next speaker is Lucia, with SLOs that survive on-call.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Burn-rate alerts and error budgets that reduce noise instead of adding to it.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Lucia covers choosing indicators, multi-window burn-rate alerts and reviewing budgets with product teams.

segments.label: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Welcome to Room A. Our next speaker is Marcus, with Closing keynote: the next five years of cloud native.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: A look ahead at where platforms, agents and open source are going.

segments.label: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Marcus closes the day with trends in platform engineering, AI-assisted operations and the community projects worth watching.
